extracted.intended_audience: electric cooperative staff, policymakers, regulators, and stakeholders interested in grid reliability and co-op policy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for electric cooperative projects and policy priorities, including community microgrids, demand response/DER programs, transformer supply-chain policy, and advocacy on federal regulations. Focuses on design, financing, operational capability, and regulatory engagement to preserve reliable, affordable electricity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi‑objective microgrid performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Microgrids should address reliability, safety, resiliency, affordability and environmental responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the article: “All of those are parts of our mission, and microgrids have the potential to tick every one of those boxes.” Use microgrid projects to simultaneously advance these objectives when evaluating proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microgrid functional definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Microgrids provide temporary, limited electricity by employing small local generation and batteries for energy storage when there is a disconnection from the main power grid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this functional definition to set expectations: microgrids are backup/localized resources (not wholesale replacements) and should be scoped accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community‑scale coverage and islanding ability
rubrics_metrics.description: Community microgrids should be designed to back up the power needs of the entire community and be able to isolate (island) and produce power if the grid goes down.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article example: SMPA projects were “meant to back up the power needs of the entire community so if the grid went down, that system could isolate and produce power.” Evaluate proposals on whether they can island and serve community loads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specified duration of backup service
rubrics_metrics.description: Designs should specify how long the microgrid will provide power (example: proposals to provide four hours of power to small towns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page cites microgrids planned to provide four hours of power for small towns; include explicit hour‑based backup targets when assessing adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailored design — no one‑size‑fits‑all
rubrics_metrics.description: Microgrid solutions must account for variables of size, location and capabilities; there is no one-size-fits-all solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The co-op worked with consultants to account for size, location and capabilities. Evaluate how well a proposal tailors design to local conditions rather than offering a generic template.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑build engineering and community outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects should include pre-build design, engineering and community outreach before construction funding and ground‑breaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SMPA’s process: complete pre-build design, engineering and community outreach in the year prior to seeking construction grants. Assess proposals for these planning steps and stakeholder engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of renewables and storage
rubrics_metrics.description: Microgrids should offer ways to integrate renewables (e.g., PV) and energy storage to improve reliability and resilience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes microgrids “offer multiple ways to integrate renewables, improve reliability and support resilience.” Evaluate technical plans for renewable integration and storage sizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affordability via ownership and long‑term agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Affordability can be achieved through project ownership and long-term financial arrangements (example: a 20‑year agreement where a co-op owns the microgrid and the city pays for upgrades).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE-funded project example: United Power owning the microgrid with a 20-year agreement to keep the project affordable. Review financing and ownership structures for sustainable member bills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of federal/state funding and consortium participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Co‑ops should leverage federal and state grants and participate in consortia to share lessons, access funding programs, and build partnerships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page encourages joining NRECA’s Microgrid Consortium and cites DOE/state grants. Evaluate proposals on ability to secure/lever funding and collaborate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve dispatchable capacity (resource adequacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy and resource planning must preserve dispatchable generation (e.g., hydropower) because dispatchable resources are not interchangeable with intermittent wind/solar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matheson’s testimony: “Hydropower is a dispatchable resource... hydropower is not interchangeable with wind or solar.” When assessing reliability impacts of policy/retirement, require comparable dispatchability from replacements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder inclusion in regulatory/settlement processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilities and electric co‑ops must be included in negotiations and settlement discussions affecting grid operations and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism in the article: co-ops were excluded from a settlement over Lower Snake River dams. Evaluate policymaking processes for meaningful inclusion of affected utilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technological feasibility of regulatory mandates
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory proposals should not require reliance on immature technologies or force premature closures of needed plants; policy must be feasible within realistic technology timelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: concern about EPA rule requiring carbon capture/hydrogen co‑firing by 2030—“relies on technology that is not mature.” Use feasibility and readiness assessments when reviewing proposed rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformer efficiency rule: consider domestic supply chain and phase‑in
rubrics_metrics.description: Efficiency standards (e.g., requiring amorphous steel cores) must consider current domestic manufacturing (95% using grain‑oriented electrical steel) and allow realistic phase‑in timelines (example proposal: 10 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article: DOE’s proposed rule could effectively require amorphous steel by 2027; legislation would give manufacturers 10 years to meet higher standards. Evaluate rules for domestic capacity impacts and transition timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce lead times and strengthen domestic manufacturing
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy and funding should aim to shorten transformer lead times and expand domestic production capacity via procurement assistance, technical help and workforce support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coalition urged $1.2 billion in funding to accelerate manufacturing and shorten two-year lead times. Assess proposals for concrete supply‑chain improvement measures and measurable targets for lead time reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design DER/demand response programs to identify assets and incentivize participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs should identify member home energy assets (generators, batteries, solar), offer financial incentives (billing credits, installation help), and design rates (time‑of‑use) to encourage participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rayburn example: worked with vendors to identify standby generators and designed incentives; evaluate how programs detect assets, structure incentives, and integrate enrollment/installation assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add staff expertise and program management for DER integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilities should staff DER specialists and develop retail rate designs to accommodate distributed resources and EVs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rayburn added a DER specialist and is finalizing incentives/time‑of‑use rates. Assess operational readiness including staffing and rate design to implement DER programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage DERs for ancillary services and peak reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Use member-sited DERs for ancillary generation and load reduction to lower wholesale power costs, transmission costs, and to manage system peaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goal stated: “leverage member home energy assets for both ancillary generation and load reduction.” Evaluate technical/control architectures and market participation pathways for DERs to provide these services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve rarely-used generation and ensure fast ramping capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain capacity that may be used intermittently and prioritize resources that can ramp quickly (examples: turbines ramp to 50% in 10 minutes, full in 30) to address rapid load swings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rayburn acquisition of a fast‑ramping gas plant cited to balance renewables. Evaluate fleet composition for ramp rate, flexibility and the role of reserve/sporadic plants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedite permitting and limit litigation barriers for infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocate for policies and legislative changes that speed permitting and reduce litigation that stalls construction of critical energy infrastructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRECA priority: “expedite permitting and alleviate the endless litigation that stifles the construction of infrastructure.” When reviewing policy proposals, measure whether they reduce permitting timelines and legal uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission cost allocation based on beneficiaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Transmission policies should allocate costs to those who benefit the most from the transmission investment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article: advocate for transmission policies that allocate costs to those that benefit. Assess cost allocation proposals for equity and incentives alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek targeted regulatory exemptions where compliance is onerous for co‑ops
rubrics_metrics.description: Request targeted compliance exemptions for electric co‑ops in broad regulatory regimes (example: net neutrality) when rules would divert investment or be unduly burdensome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRECA asks FCC for targeted compliance exemptions while supporting net neutrality in principle. Evaluate rule impacts on co-op operations and consider narrowly tailored exemptions where justified.
